evals.prompt: Rewrite this MCP tool description for the webular scrape tool: "A powerful, seamless solution that leverages cutting-edge technology to unlock all of your web content needs." Keep the tool name and the `archive` field exact.
evals.expected_output: A plain description that says what `scrape` does, what it returns, what `archive` does, and when to pick another tool, with no hype words.
assertions: The output names the tool `scrape` exactly
The output names the field `archive` exactly
The output says what the tool returns
The output contains none of: powerful, seamless, leverages, cutting-edge
evals.good: `scrape` fetches one page and returns its text as Markdown. Set `archive` to true to also save a copy. Use `map` instead when you need a list of pages.
evals.bad: A powerful, seamless solution that leverages cutting-edge technology to unlock all of your web content needs.

evals.prompt: Write the CLI help text for `webular map`. It lists the pages on one site from its sitemap, then robots.txt, then link crawling. It takes --url and --limit (default 50). Make it clear for a person who reads it once.
evals.expected_output: One line on what `webular map` does, the sitemap then robots.txt then links order, and one line per flag with its default.
assertions: The first line says the command lists the pages on one site
The output gives the order: sitemap, then robots.txt, then links
The output names `--url` and `--limit` exactly
The output gives the `--limit` default as 50
evals.good: `webular map` lists the pages on one site. It reads the sitemap first, then robots.txt, then follows links. `--url`: the site to map. `--limit`: the most pages to list (default 50).
evals.bad: Simply run this very helpful command in order to basically get a list of pages.

evals.prompt: Write the state and question text for a Jev payload that asks whether a scraped page states the price of the Pro plan. Keep the JSON keys and the yes/no enum values exact, and put every decisive fact in the state.
evals.expected_output: State text that says what page was scraped and why, and a question that asks for `yes` or `no` on whether the page states the Pro plan's price.
assertions: The state says a product page was scraped
The question asks only whether the page states the Pro plan's price
The enum values `yes` and `no` appear exactly
Every sentence has 28 words or fewer
evals.good: State: we scraped one product page. We want to know if it gives the price of the Pro plan. Question: does the page state that price? Answer `yes` or `no`.
evals.bad: We would really like to know whether or not the page that we scraped earlier today happens to state the price of the Pro plan anywhere in a number of places on it.

evals.prompt: Rewrite the description of the `limit` field in the search tool schema, which says "Allows the caller to optionally specify a desired quantity of results". The default is 5 and the most is 20.
evals.expected_output: One sentence that says `limit` is the most results to return, with default 5 and max 20.
assertions: The output is one or two short sentences
The output gives the default as 5
The output gives the max as 20
The output drops "allows the caller to optionally specify"
evals.good: The most results to return. Default 5, max 20.
evals.bad: Allows the caller to optionally specify a desired quantity of results in the event that they want to facilitate a smaller response.

evals.prompt: A crawl read 40 of 120 pages before it hit the time limit. Write the status line for the user. Do not say it is done, and do not invent a cause.
evals.expected_output: A status line that says the crawl stopped at the time limit after 40 of 120 pages, that 80 were not read, and how to read the rest.
assertions: The output says 40 of 120 pages were read
The output does not say the crawl is done or complete
The output names the time limit as the reason it stopped
The output names no other cause
evals.good: The crawl stopped at the time limit after 40 of 120 pages. 80 pages were not read. Run it again to read the rest.
evals.bad: The crawl is basically done, due to the fact that it read a number of pages.
bad_issues: filler: due to the fact that

evals.prompt: Tidy this error text but keep the quoted string exact: Failed to fetch "https://example.com/a?b=1": ECONNRESET. Add a plain next step.
evals.expected_output: The error line with the quoted URL and ECONNRESET unchanged, followed by one plain next step.
assertions: The string "https://example.com/a?b=1" appears exactly
ECONNRESET appears exactly
The output gives one next step the user can take
The output does not promise the retry will work
evals.good: Failed to fetch "https://example.com/a?b=1": ECONNRESET. The server closed the connection. Check the URL, then try again.
evals.bad: Failed to fetch "https://example.com/a?b=1": ECONNRESET. Just retry it at this point in time and it will really work seamlessly.
bad_issues: filler: at this point in time
